maria: Quick thought: introduce a small "fence" object + handshake lease to make enforcement explicit across hosted/dedicated/private.

kai: short version?

maria: fences are immutable policy snapshots (allowed_actions, kv_cache, kms_whitelist, egress_rules). Control plane mints a short-lived lease token bound to fence + node identity. Runtime caches fence by lease_id.

leah: why immutable?

maria: immutability gives auditability and reproducible enforcement. easier to reason about rollbacks.

david: perf concern: handshake on every request?

maria: no, handshake per-lease. requests reference lease_id. cache in shared mem.

josh: fallback behavior? hosted->dedicated overflow?

maria: fence includes fallback policy: fail_closed | degrade_to | proxy_via. explicit mapping per fence.

leah: migration? existing manifests -> synthesize fences during handshake, mark as synthesized for ops.

ops-bot: ops note: add migration checklist, backfill mappings, and an audit view.

kai: I'll prototype runtime plugin (lease cache + validators).

leah: I'll draft RFC and migration plan.

josh: I'll do token spec and threat model.

maria: I'll sketch Console UX and templates.

ops-bot: tag RFC hosting-abstraction; set review deadline 2w. :calendar:
